task_description:
# Token-Budget-Aware Chunk Packing for Retrieval

## Background
An offline retrieval service must ingest a small heterogeneous document corpus and turn it into
embedding-ready chunks. Every chunk has to stay inside a hard token budget of the embedding model,
must carry its section context and provenance, and the whole artifact has to be byte-for-byte
reproducible so that downstream index builds can be cached.

The container is fully air-gapped. Docling is pre-installed (CPU only, all model weights baked into
the image) and a HuggingFace tokenizer directory is baked in as well. Do not install packages,
download models, or contact any network service.

## Requirements
Build a single-file command line tool `chunkpack.py` that converts, chunks, and audits the local
corpus:

- Convert every supported source document in the corpus and split it into chunks whose size is
  governed by a token budget measured with the baked-in tokenizer.
- Emit one contextualized chunk record per line into a JSONL artifact, plus an aggregate summary.
- Guarantee the budget: no emitted chunk may exceed it, including documents that contain a single
  element far larger than the budget, deeply nested section hierarchies, and tables.
- Never drop content: every whitespace-separated word of a document's textual content (including
  table cell values) must appear in that document's emitted chunk texts.
- Expose a self-audit subcommand that re-validates an existing artifact directory.

## Implementation Hints
- Project path: `/home/user/chunkforge`. Create `chunkpack.py` there.
- Corpus (read-only input, do not modify or add files): `/home/user/chunkforge/assets/corpus`.
- Tokenizer: `/home/user/chunkforge/assets/tokenizer`. This local directory is the only tokenizer
  allowed; all token counting must be done with it.
- Commands (always run with the project path as the working directory):
  - `python3 chunkpack.py pack --corpus <dir> --out <dir> --max-tokens <int> [--no-merge-peers]`
  - `python3 chunkpack.py verify --out <dir>`
- `--corpus`, `--out` and `--max-tokens` are mandatory for `pack`. `--no-merge-peers` is optional:
  by default undersized neighbouring chunks that share the same section context are merged together
  while staying inside the budget; when the flag is given that merging must be switched off.
- Source discovery: search `--corpus` recursively. Supported extensions (case-insensitive):
  `.md`, `.html`, `.docx`, `.pdf`. Every other file is ignored for chunking and recorded as skipped.
  A source is identified by its POSIX relative path with respect to the `--corpus` directory
  (e.g. `appendix/omega_notes.md`). All source orderings are ascending by that string.
- `pack` writes exactly two artifacts into `--out` (creating the directory when missing and
  replacing any previous content of these two files): `chunks.jsonl` and `summary.json`.
- `chunks.jsonl` is UTF-8, LF-terminated (no carriage returns), one JSON object per line, with a
  trailing newline after the last object. Chunks are grouped per source in ascending source order,
  and inside a source they keep the order in which the document is read. Each object has exactly
  these nine keys:
  - `chunk_id` (string): `"<source>#<ordinal>"` where `<ordinal>` is zero-padded to 4 digits
    (e.g. `alpha_guide.md#0003`).
  - `index` (integer): 0-based position of the chunk within the whole run; the values on the lines
    must be `0, 1, 2, ...` in ascending order.
  - `source` (string): POSIX relative path of the source document.
  - `ordinal` (integer): 0-based position of the chunk within its own source document.
  - `heading_path` (array of non-empty strings): the section-title ancestry of the chunk, outermost
    title first; an empty array when the chunk has no section context.
  - `page_numbers` (array of integers): ascending, duplicate-free page numbers the chunk's content
    comes from; an empty array when the source format carries no page provenance.
  - `token_count` (integer): the number of tokens the baked-in tokenizer produces for the value of
    `text` (plain tokenization, no special/added tokens counted).
  - `is_partial_element` (boolean): `true` when the chunk carries only a portion of one single
    source element whose content had to be divided across several chunks to respect the budget,
    `false` otherwise.
  - `text` (string): the contextualized chunk text. When `heading_path` is non-empty the text must
    begin with those headings, one per line and in order, followed by a newline and then the chunk
    body; the body must not be empty or whitespace-only. When `heading_path` is empty the text is
    the body alone.
- Budget rule: for every emitted chunk `0 < token_count <= --max-tokens`, without exception. You may
  assume that for the provided corpus and any budget of at least 32 tokens the heading prefix plus
  one body word always fits.
- `summary.json` is UTF-8 JSON with exactly these top-level keys:
  - `tokenizer_path` (string): absolute path of the tokenizer directory used.
  - `max_tokens` (integer): the budget of this run.
  - `merge_peers` (boolean): whether peer merging was active in this run.
  - `documents` (array): one object per successfully chunked source, ascending by `source`, each
    with exactly the keys `source` (string), `chunk_count` (integer), `token_total` (integer, sum of
    the document's `token_count` values), `max_chunk_tokens` (integer, 0 when the document produced
    no chunk), `mean_chunk_tokens` (number, `token_total / chunk_count` rounded to 2 decimals, 0.0
    when the document produced no chunk), `partial_chunk_count` (integer, number of chunks of that
    document with `is_partial_element` true), `max_heading_depth` (integer, longest `heading_path`
    of that document, 0 when none), `page_numbers` (array of integers, ascending duplicate-free
    union of the document's chunk page numbers).
  - `totals` (object) with exactly the keys `document_count`, `chunk_count`, `token_total`,
    `partial_chunk_count` and `budget_violations`, all integers; `budget_violations` counts emitted
    chunks whose `token_count` exceeds `max_tokens` and must therefore be 0.
  - `skipped_files` (array of strings): ascending POSIX relative paths of corpus files ignored
    because of an unsupported extension.
- On success `pack` exits 0 and the last non-empty line it writes to stdout is exactly
  `PACKED documents=<D> chunks=<C> max_tokens=<M> merge_peers=<true|false>` with `<D>`, `<C>` and
  `<M>` matching the summary and the boolean spelled in lowercase.
- `verify --out <dir>` re-reads `<dir>/chunks.jsonl` together with `<dir>/summary.json` (taking the
  budget and the tokenizer location from the summary) and re-checks: valid JSON lines carrying
  exactly the nine required keys; `token_count` equal to a freshly computed token count of `text`;
  `token_count` within the budget; `index` values forming `0..N-1` in ascending order; per-source
  ordinals forming `0..k-1` in ascending order; and `chunk_id` matching the `source`/`ordinal`
  spelling. When everything holds it exits 0 and writes a line starting with `VERIFIED` to stdout.
  When at least one check fails it exits 3, writes nothing containing `VERIFIED` to stdout, and
  writes at least one line starting with `VIOLATION` to stderr.
- Failure handling: exit code 2 with a message beginning with `ERROR` on stderr when the `--corpus`
  directory does not exist, when `--max-tokens` is not an integer of at least 32, or when `verify`
  is pointed at a directory that lacks `chunks.jsonl` or `summary.json`. Exit codes 0, 2 and 3 are
  the only ones the tool may return.
- Determinism: two runs of the same command must produce byte-identical `chunks.jsonl` and
  `summary.json`; nothing time-, host- or randomness-dependent may appear in the artifacts.
- Finally, run the tool once and leave its artifacts in the repository:
  `python3 chunkpack.py pack --corpus assets/corpus --out out --max-tokens 128`
  so that `/home/user/chunkforge/out/chunks.jsonl` and `/home/user/chunkforge/out/summary.json`
  exist and are up to date.

truth:
# Verification Plan

## Setup
1. Work in `/home/user/chunkforge`.
2. Do not delete `/home/user/chunkforge/out` - it is a required deliverable. All verification runs
   that create files must write into fresh temporary directories under `/tmp` (removed and
   recreated at the beginning of each check that uses them).
3. A mini corpus is used for the fast checks: copy only `assets/corpus/alpha_guide.md` into a fresh
   temporary directory (e.g. `/tmp/mini_corpus`).

## Verification Steps
1. **Deliverables exist**: `chunkpack.py`, `out/chunks.jsonl` and `out/summary.json` exist under
   `/home/user/chunkforge`; `chunks.jsonl` is non-empty, ends with a newline and contains no `\r`.
2. **Record schema**: every line of `out/chunks.jsonl` parses as a JSON object whose key set is
   exactly {`chunk_id`, `index`, `source`, `ordinal`, `heading_path`, `page_numbers`,
   `token_count`, `is_partial_element`, `text`} with the documented types; every `text` has a
   non-whitespace body; every heading entry is a non-empty string; every page number is an integer
   >= 1 and each `page_numbers` array is strictly ascending.
3. **Ordering and identifiers**: `index` values are `0..N-1` in file order; the lines of a source
   are contiguous; the sources appear in ascending order; per-source `ordinal` values are `0..k-1`;
   `chunk_id` equals `f"{source}#{ordinal:04d}"`.
4. **Source selection**: the set of `source` values is exactly
   {`alpha_guide.md`, `appendix/omega_notes.md`, `beta_report.html`, `delta_brief.pdf`,
   `gamma_minutes.docx`}, and `summary.json`'s `skipped_files` is exactly `["notes.txt"]`.
5. **Budget**: every `token_count` is > 0 and <= 128.
6. **Token counts are real**: loading `/home/user/chunkforge/assets/tokenizer` with
   `transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` and tokenizing each `text` yields exactly the
   stored `token_count` for every chunk.
7. **Heading contract and deep nesting**: for each chunk the first `len(heading_path)` lines of
   `text` equal `heading_path`, and the remaining text is non-empty; at least one chunk of
   `alpha_guide.md` has a `heading_path` of length >= 4.
8. **Summary aggregates**: `summary.json` has exactly the documented top-level keys;
   `tokenizer_path` is `/home/user/chunkforge/assets/tokenizer`, `max_tokens` is 128,
   `merge_peers` is true; `documents` is ordered by `source` and each entry's `chunk_count`,
   `token_total`, `max_chunk_tokens`, `partial_chunk_count`, `max_heading_depth` and `page_numbers`
   match a recomputation from `chunks.jsonl`, with `mean_chunk_tokens` within 0.01 of
   `token_total / chunk_count`; `totals` matches the recomputation and `budget_violations` is 0.
9. **Oversized element handling**: `alpha_guide.md` contains a single paragraph much larger than
   128 tokens, so it must yield at least two chunks with `is_partial_element` true, all of them
   inside the budget; the marker words `ZQXSENTINELALPHA`, `ZQXSENTINELMIDDLE` and
   `ZQXSENTINELOMEGA` that occur in that paragraph must each appear in the chunk texts of
   `alpha_guide.md` (no content dropped).
10. **Table content preserved**: the chunk texts of `beta_report.html` contain the strings
    `Region`, `Zurich` and `18420` (header label and a body cell of the table in that document).
11. **Page provenance**: at least one chunk of `delta_brief.pdf` has a non-empty `page_numbers`
    array, and every page number of that document is 1 (the PDF has a single page).
12. **stdout contract and determinism**: run
    `python3 chunkpack.py pack --corpus assets/corpus --out /tmp/rerun --max-tokens 128`;
    it exits 0, the last non-empty stdout line equals
    `PACKED documents=5 chunks=<C> max_tokens=128 merge_peers=true` where `<C>` is the number of
    lines of `out/chunks.jsonl`, and `/tmp/rerun/chunks.jsonl` and `/tmp/rerun/summary.json` are
    byte-identical to the committed ones in `out/`.
13. **Idempotence**: running
    `python3 chunkpack.py pack --corpus /tmp/mini_corpus --out /tmp/mini_a --max-tokens 96` twice
    into the same output directory leaves byte-identical artifacts both times.
14. **Peer merging switch**: run the mini corpus with `--max-tokens 96` once without and once with
    `--no-merge-peers` (into separate temporary directories). Both runs exit 0, `summary.json`'s
    `merge_peers` is true resp. false, every chunk stays within 96 tokens, and the run with
    `--no-merge-peers` produces strictly more chunks (the document has six consecutive short
    paragraphs under one heading that merge into fewer chunks when merging is on).
15. **Budget scaling**: run the mini corpus with `--max-tokens 64` and with `--max-tokens 256`.
    Both exit 0, every chunk respects its own budget, and the 64-token run produces strictly more
    chunks than the 256-token run.
16. **verify accepts a valid artifact**: `python3 chunkpack.py verify --out out` exits 0 and prints
    a line starting with `VERIFIED`.
17. **verify rejects tampering**: copy `out/` to a temporary directory and (a) increase one chunk's
    `token_count` by 1000, (b) in a second copy replace one `chunk_id` with `bogus#0000`, (c) in a
    third copy delete the `page_numbers` key from one line. Each tampered directory must make
    `verify` exit 3, print a line starting with `VIOLATION` on stderr and print no `VERIFIED` on
    stdout.
18. **Usage errors**: `pack --corpus assets/corpus --out /tmp/x --max-tokens 8` exits 2 with a
    stderr message starting with `ERROR`; `pack --corpus assets/does_not_exist --out /tmp/x
    --max-tokens 128` exits 2 with a stderr message starting with `ERROR`; `verify --out` on an
    empty temporary directory exits 2 with a stderr message starting with `ERROR`.
